title: Press Inquiry Committee 1947
definition: The Press Inquiry Committee (1947) was a post-independence government initiative tasked with reviewing the existing restrictive press laws inherited from the British colonial administration to align them with the democratic aspirations of a free India.
importanceInUpsc: It serves as a critical bridge between colonial-era press censorship and the constitutional guarantee of Freedom of Speech and Expression (Article 19(1)(a)), often tested in the context of the evolution of media laws in India.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Press Inquiry Committee 1947.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
